purpose: Independent practice of B2.2 (facts to 20) and B2.3 (mental strategies to 50). Captures diagnostic-level evidence for the unit.
student_learning_goal: I can recall addition facts to 20 and use mental strategies to add and subtract within 50.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can recall addition facts to 20 and use mental strategies to add and subtract within 50.
header.character_watermark: Mae the Multiplier in the top-right corner with × symbol patches on her apron. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Fill in each fact. Watch for doubles and near-doubles.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. An 8-row table with a fact on each row.

image_placeholders.description: An 8-row fact-fluency table in B&W line-art. Each row has two pre-filled addend boxes and a blank sum box. Rows: 6+6, 7+7, 8+8, 9+9, 10+10, 5+6, 7+8, 8+9.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_FACTS_TABLE: keywords (doubles, near-doubles) name what the table shows.

parts.student_instructions: Each double ten-frame shows the starting position. Draw the make-ten arrow. Write the equation chain.
parts.visual_layout: Upper-middle. Four double ten-frame scenes in a 2x2 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Four double ten-frame scenes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 2-column grid. Each scene shows a top ten-frame and a bottom ten-frame stacked. Pre-fills: TF1 — top 8 red, bottom 5 red (8+5); TF2 — top 9 red, bottom 6 red (9+6); TF3 — top 7 red, bottom 5 red (7+5); TF4 — top 9 red, bottom 7 red (9+7). Below each scene, an equation chain.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_FOUR_TEN_FRAMES: keywords (ten-frame, make-ten) name what the scenes show.

parts.student_instructions: Chunk each number into tens and ones. Add the tens. Add the ones. Combine.
parts.visual_layout: Middle-lower. Four chunking problems in a 2x2 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Four chunking-by-tens problem boxes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 2-column grid. Each box ~3in × 1.5in. Format per box: problem on top (e.g., '32 + 15 = ?'); chunked working area below ('30+2 + 10+5 = ___ + ___ = ___'); answer line. Problems: 32+15, 47+22, 65-30, 38-15.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_FOUR_CHUNKS: keywords (chunk, tens) name the problem layout.

parts.student_instructions: For each fact, circle the strategy you would use.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom. Four rows. Each row has a fact and four strategy bubbles.

image_placeholders.description: Four rows in B&W line-art. Each row ~7in wide. Format: fact box on left, four strategy bubbles to the right (DOUBLE / NEAR-DOUBLE / MAKE-TEN / CHUNK-BY-TENS). Facts: 7+7, 9+5, 32+15, 5+12.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P4_STRATEGY_CHOICE: keywords (strategy, choice) name what the rows ask for.

parts.answer_key: 7+7: DOUBLE. 9+5: MAKE-TEN. 32+15: CHUNK-BY-TENS. 5+12: NEAR-DOUBLE (or accept count-on for 5+12).

parts.student_instructions: Mae has 28 paper kittens. Buddy delivers 15 more. How many kittens? Show the chunk-by-tens working.
parts.visual_layout: Speech bubble from Mae stating the story; below, a 4-row chunk-by-tens working frame: 'Tens: ___ + ___ = ___' / 'Ones: ___ + ___ = ___' / 'Combine: ___ + ___ = ___' / 'Total: ___'.
parts.answer_key: Tens: 20+10=30; Ones: 8+5=13; Combine: 30+13=43. Total: 43 kittens. Accept any chunk-by-tens working that arrives at 43.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write THREE chunk-by-tens problems of your own and solve them.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Use Part 3 as the strongest evidence for B2.3 chunking — children who can articulate the four-step chunk move are at L4. Watch for: Part 1 fluency gaps (children who slow down on 7+8 or 8+9 need a doubles drill); Part 3 children who default to count-all (need explicit chunking reteach). Part 5 added as TRANSFER probe — story problem requiring chunk-by-tens working. Verifies strategy generalises beyond lesson examples.
